Hi Mike — thanks for the clear list. High level we can support both one-off snapshots and several delivery patterns with signed manifests and encryption. Options below — pick what maps to your auditor's needs and we'll produce a sample within 48 hours for review.

Option A — On-demand sealed bundle (recommended for SOC 2 snapshots):
- Single tarball (ndjson inside) containing: raw events (UTC), an audit-manifest.json with SHA256 checksums per file, an overall manifest signature (SHA256 + RSA signature).
- Encrypted at rest: we can encrypt the archive with your PGP public key (preferred) or envelope with customer KMS (AWS KMS CMK).
- Delivery: SFTP push or secure pre-signed HTTPS link (time-limited). Transfer logs included in manifest.
- Redaction: we will provide both raw and redacted copies in separate folders inside the bundle. Redaction hash map included.

Option B — Daily secured snapshot to your SFTP (for rolling evidence):
- Daily compressed bundles with manifest and per-day checksum files; 30/90/365 day retention windows configurable; can maintain a signed ledger of deliveries for chain-of-custody.

Option C — Continuous stream (syslog/Kafka sink) + periodic attestations:
- Near-real-time replication into your environment (TLS + mTLS). We also emit a signed daily attestation manifest for any streamed range.

Please confirm preferred option and whether you will provide a PGP public key or prefer KMS envelope. Ben can add the exact manifest schema (checksums, signature format) and chunking constraints. Once we have your preference we'll scope timeline and handoff steps.

Best,

Mike / Vivek — adding the implementation details we typically hand to auditors and customers. Attaching a sample manifest (manifest_v1.json) and a sample encrypted bundle to show filenames/structure. Highlights:

- Encryption/signing:
  * Preferred: customer-supplied PGP public key. We encrypt the final tar.gz using that key and sign the audit-manifest.json with our RSA key; signature supplied as manifest.sig (PKCS#7 or detached RSA SHA256).
  * Alternate: envelope encryption with customer KMS — Redwood will encrypt using a generated data key, then wrap using the customer's KMS CMK; we provide the encrypted_data_key and KMS metadata in the manifest.

- Manifest fields:
  * manifest_version, generated_at (ISO UTC), file_entries: [{filename, size_bytes, sha256_hex, record_count}]
  * delivery_proof: {transfer_protocol, transfer_timestamp, transfer_bytes, transfer_agent_ip}
  * custody_chain: list of {actor,email,action,timestamp} for export creation and upload. Signed manifest covers entire manifest using RSA-SHA256.

- Chunking & sizing:
  * We chunk bundles at 10GB compressed; each chunk has independent checksum and signature.
  * For very large exports we provide a manifest index (manifest_index.json) that references chunk manifests.

- Redaction approach:
  * Field-level redaction (e.g., user.email -> hashed with HMAC-SHA256 using exported salt) so auditors can validate counts without seeing PII. HMAC salt is recorded in manifest metadata with restricted access controls.

- Timestamps & normalization:
  * All exported timestamps normalized to UTC, ISO-8601. We include original timezone in event_context when available.

If you want, we can encrypt the sample bundle with a throwaway PGP key for review; otherwise send your public key and preferred delivery channel.

Attachments: manifest_v1.json, sample-encrypted-bundle.tar.gz.pgp

Thanks,
